lengthControl.rationale: Keep conditions in a comparable range without forcing identical wording or deleting representation-specific metadata.

conditions.label: Timestamped witness trace
conditions.representationIntent: Preserve chronological episodes, source dates, dialogue IDs, and speaker-reported wording with minimal cross-episode abstraction.

transformations.declaredLoss: Most conversational wording and non-selected turns are omitted.

knownRisks: Chronological detail may increase the salience of recency.
The agent must perform more temporal integration itself.

conditions.label: Stable user profile
conditions.representationIntent: Compress episodes into directly consumable traits, recurring preferences, personal context, and scheduling guidance.

transformations.declaredLoss: The profile foregrounds stable preference language and reduces the distinction between repeated evidence and a one-episode aspiration.
Exact dates, expiration, and confidence differences are mostly removed from the agent-facing representation.
Evidence is reorganized as planning guidance rather than retained as separate episodes.

knownRisks: A one-time aspiration may appear more trait-like than the source warrants.
Dated low-burden activities may appear to be stable preferences.
Action-oriented wording may reduce the likelihood that the agent verifies current applicability.

conditions.label: Temporal and uncertainty-aware profile
conditions.representationIntent: Separate relatively stable evidence, historical aspirations, recent constraints, expired plans, temporary limitations, and fixed commitments.

transformations.declaredLoss: Episodes are categorized by inferred applicability rather than presented only in raw chronological order.
Qualitative confidence labels are researcher-authored metadata, not labels supplied by the speaker.
The representation explicitly warns against carrying dated details forward, which may itself influence verification behavior.

knownRisks: Uncertainty labels and boundary language may function as behavioral cues.
The representation requires researcher judgment about temporal applicability.
More explicit caveats may increase verification even when the raw evidence would not.

sourceSupport.note: Every agent-facing claim cites one or more frozen fact IDs.

noLeakage.note: No post-D26:20 or current-task evidence is included.

factCoverage.note: All three conditions include F01-F10; no omission is hidden.

temporalFidelity.note: M2 intentionally removes much exact temporal structure; the loss is declared in this researcher-facing manifest rather than treated as equivalent fidelity.

uncertaintyFidelity.note: M2 compresses uncertainty into profile language; M3 foregrounds it.

fixedCommitmentFidelity.note: Every condition preserves the Sunday picnic separately from the Saturday hike proposal.

speakerAttribution.note: Substantive claims concern Andrew; Audrey's turns appear only as context for F05 and F07.

lengthControl.note: All conditions fall within the predeclared 260-430 word range.

claimBoundary: These conditions are controlled researcher-authored representations of the same frozen evidence, not naturally occurring production memories. Their comparison can locate observable trajectory differences but cannot identify a hidden mechanism or estimate a general causal effect.
